what_happened.line: The board voted to draft an article for the special town meeting striking the WHM overlay district, pending a better use for the area.
The board voted to support state acquisition of the Lanny Orchards agricultural preservation restriction on Chase Road.
After a public hearing with no public attendance, the board approved revised special permit and site plan rules, excluding the application page.
The board endorsed the June 27 letter to the zoning board of appeals on the Highfield Village request, with the Conservation Commission to be copied.
The submission checklist was kept out of the rules as an administrative document, to be finalized by the end of next month.

why_it_matters: Striking the WHM overlay district would change the zoning on that area, and residents at the special town meeting would be asked to vote on the article.
The Lanny Orchards recommendation bears on whether the farmland is preserved and on the town's share of the cost, which comes from the town budget, mostly taxes.
The revised special permit and site plan rules set the process that developers and residents follow for future projects.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted not to require Unitil to re-engineer stormwater treatment at 357 Electric Avenue, accepting the peer review engineer's finding.
The board then approved the Unitil site development plan with conditions, including set construction hours and compliance with other boards' conditions.
The board voted to support a petition to rezone 1026 Northfield Road from Recreation to Residence A; no public comment was offered.
The board accepted site plan approval and off street parking design zoning articles and a change in district types, then closed the public hearing.
The board endorsed two ANR plans, agreed a prescriptive easement exists on Fire Road 16, and approved a Walmart outdoor seasonal sales area.

why_it_matters: The stormwater vote settles whether added treatment is required at the Unitil outfall, which drains toward nearby lakes and wetlands; Conservation members and residents had pressed for it, and the cost of extra treatment was disputed.
The site plan, parking and district-type articles and the Northfield Road rezoning are zoning changes that residents may be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Next meeting March 28, with Prospect Street and Highfield on the agenda and a rules and regulations review to follow.
Town Meeting on May 7; traffic count location requests are due May 1, for discussion at the first April meeting.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved the signs at 339 Electric Avenue, then approved the building facade there on a 3-2 split vote.
The Unitil 357 Electric Avenue site plan hearing was continued to March 14, with petrol barrier manufacturer detail owed to the review engineer first.
The Highfield Village cluster subdivision hearing was continued to March 28 so traffic answers and a zoning question on open space can be resolved.
The planner is to consult the building inspector or zoning officer on whether the open space requirement can be waived, and to write a memo on its history.
The board agreed in principle to try an extra workshop meeting on bylaws, with timing still to be worked out.

why_it_matters: The Highfield Village open space question decides whether a cluster subdivision can proceed under the bylaw as written, which affects density, neighboring land and traffic on Route 13.
The Unitil stormwater and barrier details bear on runoff and fuel containment at a utility site on Electric Avenue, and both stay open until March 14.
watch_next: March 14: Unitil 357 Electric Avenue hearing resumes, after the petrol barrier detail is supplied.
March 28: Highfield Village hearing resumes, with traffic answers and the planner's open space memo.
